title: The round fan-out ignores the model each node reports, so nodes running another model get the task and always fail.
Fleet nodes share the single admin WORKER_TOKEN, and node identity is whatever node_id the request body claims, so any device can impersonate others and approve human-gated jobs
FedAvg trusts the example count each node reports and never checks adapter contents, so one node can publish a NaN, attacker-chosen or corrupt global adapter
MCP tools return node-controlled text without the untrusted-output note, and node metrics strings have no length limit
The node registry has no cap, so a single broadcast_prompt can fan out to unlimited fake nodes while every heartbeat rewrites the whole registry under the fleet lock
